      {
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past purchases and listening as continuing interest in broadly related items, with insufficient attention to what users would choose next.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Close connections to recurring artists, musical styles and story themes provide recognizable reasons to choose recommendations.",
    "Accessories and supplies align when they support an established activity or add a useful capability to existing equipment."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related products and adjacent entertainment styles compete with stronger matches to users' specific purposes, sounds and themes.",
    "Recent ownership is treated as evidence for buying similar devices or supplies, even when the purchase has already satisfied that need.",
    "Older or seasonal interests remain influential when recent behavior suggests a different immediate priority."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared brands, product families and broad domains substitute for evidence of a matching function or experience.",
    "Similarity to previously purchased items is treated as sufficient reason for another purchase, overlooking duplication and diminishing usefulness."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Specific recurring preferences and recent changes in activity distinguish compelling next choices from merely plausible related items.",
    "Compatibility, quantities, existing supplies and added functionality determine whether a relevant product is actually useful.",
    "Matching tone, musical texture and subject matter matters more than broad entertainment similarity."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "The highest-ranked items too often reflect broad historical affinity rather than a specific, currently unmet reason to choose them.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked recommendations users identify as immediate choices, separated from items they merely consider relevant.",
    "The frequency of rejections attributed to duplicated capabilities, incompatible requirements or unsupported project assumptions.",
    "The frequency with which broad or older-interest matches outrank items tied to specific recurring preferences and recent activities.",
    "The share of recommendations whose fit cannot be assessed from available item information, kept separate from explicit mismatches."
  ]
}
